definition: The transfer of thermal energy through a material from its hotter part to its colder part, without the material itself moving.
A material that lets thermal energy pass through it quickly by conduction; metals such as copper are good thermal conductors.
A material that lets thermal energy pass through it only slowly by conduction, such as wood, plastic, wool or air.
An electron in a metal that is not tied to any one atom, so it can move through the metal and carry energy and electric charge.
The vibration of particles held in fixed positions in a solid, passed on from each particle to its neighbours; it carries thermal energy through every solid.
